Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag This set includes:
- Six (6) all weather colored balls of one color of each (red, yellow, orange, blue, green, and black).
- Nine (9) all weather plastic coated metal wickets.
- Six (6) solid wood mallets with wooden handles (30.75 inches assembled) --one for each color. They have double metal locking joints and assembly is required each time.
- Two (2) 24" wooden stakes with colored lines that match the colors of the balls and mallet handles. NOTE that I received four (4) wooden stakes in my package (see picture).
- One carry case.
- One paltry instruction sheet.

I had always wanted to play croquet and this is my first set. When I first opened the package, I was really impressed and considered this five stars for the price since it contains everything needed to play. In order to store all the items in the carry case, the set must be disassembled each time after play. What I mean by this is that the wooden handles have to be screwed and unscrewed from the mallet head. Since I live in a condo, I cannot leave this set assembled after playing as I have no garage to store this in and I have to remove the wickets from the complex's lawn when done with the game.

After watching some how-to videos, my boyfriend and I played this. We had a lot of fun as it is a cross between golf and bocce ball to me.

It was during play that we noticed a problem with this set. The biggest issue is that each wood mallet with its associated handle kept loosening up no matter how hard we tightened it. Several times we had to re-tighten the mallets. Also, after our game was over, we noticed that the plastic coating on the wickets was chipping off on the bottom and exposing the metal and this was the first time we used the set. I suppose this is to be expected, however..

Overall, we enjoyed this game and the set seems to be good quality with the exception of the mallet head and its associated handle loosening up. It is for this reason only I rate this 3.4 stars. A really professional set would be more than double the price of this one. If I were in the market for a higher end set, I would look into this [[ASIN:B073YFZY9M Amish-made croquet set]].
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Zebco 33 Spincast Fishing Reel, Quickset Anti-Reverse with Bite Alert, Smooth Dial-Adjustable Drag, Powerful All-Metal Gears with a Lightweight Graphite Frame Fishing is something I have enjoyed since I was very young and one of my very first reels was a spincasting Zebco 33 reel. It’s over 40 years old and it still works and I still use it, though my preference has shifted to spinning reels most of the time. This new Zebco 33 is similar in design and it works just as well (actually it’s so much newer so it works a lot more smoothly). So far I am very pleased with it.

One of the things I have appreciated about spincasting reels is their ease of use without sacrificing function. They’re easy to use, easy to understand and they do every bit as good at bringing in fish as any other type of reel. They’re a great compromise between a baitcasting reel and a spinning reel – they have the accuracy of a baitcasting reel and they do not backlash, and they’re smooth like spinning reels most of the time. This reel reflects both of those attributes. The downside I have noticed with this reel design is line memory which is especially problematic with monofilament.

This is an attractive reel, with metal covers and a graphite base. It’s much more sturdy than plastic-based reels and should hold up well over time. The handle is oversized which is probably the nicest improvement over my old 33 as retrieves are faster.

The drag is set via a dial on the top of the reel, about an inch from the button. It works very well and is easy to set. This is sometimes an issue with spincasting reels and Zebco got this right.

The bite alert is basically a reverse with a loud click as the handle spins. This works when you have an unattended pole. For some people this is probably a great feature, but for me it is a feature I am very unlikely to use most of the time. I like that it’s there, though, in case I have a need for it at some point. It’s easy to turn on and off, with a simple switch on the reel’s side.

This is the first baitcasting reel I have seen that has a reversible handle. It requires a screwdriver to switch but that’s all right – this is a great feature. I am right-handed and the reel came delivered with the handle on the right side so I don’t need to switch it, but left-handed anglers will benefit.

Casting is very smooth as is the retrieve. So far I have had absolutely no issues with this reel. It’s pre-spooled too so the first time out requires no prep work other than threading the line through the eyes on the rod, unless you need heavier or lighter line.

This is a solid and functional reel. It is a step up from my 40+ year-old vintage Zebco in terms of smoothness and functionality, and it will go with me instead of that old reel most of the time. It’s easy to understand and use and it’s well made. With some occasional maintenance there’s every reason to believe this reel will last for years of faithful service. I still prefer my spinning reel which is just a preference, but I will definitely be putting this reel to use all summer.
text_fidelity_b: Zebco 33 Spincast Fishing Reel, Quickset Anti-Reverse with Bite Alert, Smooth Dial-Adjustable Drag, Powerful All-Metal Gears with a Lightweight Graphite Frame

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) I have been using one of the original Fitbits for about five years, having received one free from my health insurance company. I had replaced that one a few times when one was lost or accidentally washed, and my most recent one had gone south.  I was a bit disappointed that the company no longer offered the original Fitbit One, so bought this to replace it. I actually love it, except for the clunkiness of the look. Because of the mechanics and sensors in it, it sits up rather higher on my wrist than a normal watch does, and I am not especially enamored of the look of the band itself. I have thought about getting one of the leather bands, as it might look a bit nicer, but all in all, the looks of the thing are the only draw back. I really like that it tracks steps, stairs, pulse and sleep without any effort on my part. While the Fitbit One tracked steps, stairs and sleep, I had to actually remember to push the button to track sleep, and it wasn’t especially accurate because it only sensed movement. With my new Fitbit Charge 2, it not only tracks sleep automatically, it also detects deep sleep, light sleep, and REM sleep based on pulse rate. I also like having the reminder that encourages me to get at least 250 steps an hour. I find that quite motivating, and enjoy the tiny, animated celebration when I meet my goal. I would have rated it five if  liked the look of it, but alas!

Therm-a-Rest Z Lite Sol Camping and Backpacking Sleeping Pad I've backpacked with this three times now and I've had good experiences with it. That said, it has major advantages and disadvantages, so you'll need to know how this fits into your camping/backpacking situation:

Pros:
- it's insanely light
- it will keep you warm from the cold ground
- it's incapable of being punctured (it's foam) so no need to worry about mid-trip repairs regarding rips

Cons:
- it is not cushy/comfortable. If you need comfort, this is not it. It's designed for weight and heat retention, not comfort
- volume. takes up more space than an inflatable mattress pad. If you have a way to strap it outside of your back this probably isn't an issue

That is all. If you're a deep sleeper and you're doing a long, ultralight trip, this is a good option. If you need more comfort and are less concerned about weight, you may want to invest in a good inflatable mattress pad

text_fidelity_a:
Direct Action Dragon Egg Tactical Backpack 25 Liter Capacity My backpack is my main go-to-always-carry-with-me bag, which is the bag I go to work with, I carry my tech in, the bag that is my "handbag", the bag I travel with, the bag I go shopping with, the bag that I bike with.
I was browsing different backpacks, that would fit my needs:
1) Separate compartment that can fit a 17-inch laptop
2) Enough organizing space for dozens of cables and tech accessories that I normally carry. Bonus if I can fit a power brick somewhere too.
3) Fits my gym gear as well
4) And a bike pump
5) Enough room for extra clothes and stuff, in case I travel with it
6) Is well balanced and easy to carry
7) Looks cool too

So I was comparing options and prices, which included {a very hyped up tactical backpack brand}, and ended up with a jet black Dragon Egg. I'm not disappointed!
1) Laptop compartment can fit my big laptop, and my iPad in a separate pocket
2) Front pocket has enough compartments for cables, accessories, and all the essentials, like phone, wallet, etc
3) Middle compartment is spacious and expandable, great for gym gear, clothes, and all the stuff
4) I can attach bike accessories to the sides or put into expandable side pockets. Also the mesh front is handy for extra lights!
5) Is sufficient as a single carry-on bag for a 1-2 day business/leisure trip. Even full loaded easily fits under airplane seat.
6) Even when fully loaded, is very easy to carry, due to good balance and padding
7) Looks great! The black color is very black and stylish. And can be customized to add more personality.

So I'm happy with it so far, it fits my needs and then some. Hope it serves me well for many years.

text_fidelity_a:
Yatoaita Stainless Steel Vacuum Insulated Wide Mouth Water Bottle,Water Bottle with Straw,Insulated Water Bottle with Straw Lid,Wide Mouth Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle (32 oz) This is a Great looking water bottle in every aspect- complete with your own tiny dancer! Whaaa...?! Men take note: this has the imprinted logo of a ballerina in a tutu smack dab on the front- I only mention this bc, having bought this for my 17yr. old to take to high school.. he was having none of it! (I guess at his awkward impressionable phase- this was just to big a risk of social suicide for him.. wow, high school hasn’t changed much!)

As for material: Comparing this next to a Hydro flask in appearance it goes toe-to-toe both, in look and style. I’m using Hydro as the measuring stick only because, it’s what all water bottles apparently aspire to be! Personally, in our house- we find water bottles can be left behind far too easy.. or, dropped/dented (compromising their thermal abilities..) so, I prefer to be smart and look for good quality at half the $- at least for The chaotic events where these vanish!!
Loving the fact this has a wide mouth. For any who aren’t certain why this matters… it’s the ability to put ice into the bottle without chiseling a cube piece by piece to fit in a small opening! This widemouth has 2 straws and one pop straw lid. Straw allows you to drink with the bottle held in place- *lid works without straw attachment… You just need to tip the bottle, this is mostly how we use! As for cleaning of straws- this comes with its own bristle brush and I included a photo the brush actually has varied direction of bristles- helping to clean out where you Cant reach and that’s a perk!! Hack: put x1 tiny drop of dish soap into straw, and scrub with brush.. then, run hot water from faucet thru straw opening for a good minute. This gets all soap remnants out and keeps next use from tasting totally soap tasty- I feel that’s always a good thing!

The lid is easy to fasten and secure. I kept this upside down x1hr. just to test for leakage- and I got none! I LOVE The handle on the lid itself.. A total bonus and 100% you will see, use and be happily surprised It’s there! Note: although I cannot personally try it… A lot of varied lids fit between different water bottles.. so, that is certainly worth a try if, wanting to trade around lids (our wide mouth hydro was our bottle just recently lost.. and what I’m replacing.. so, I cannot try swapping that lead specifically to say for sure. But, just don’t rule it out!)

As for cold drinks… This is what we use ours for and it keeps things perfectly cold. We filled with 3/4 ice and water- then, checking 24 hours later… We still had ice!! As far as water bottles go I have confidence this will perform as one hopes it would, tiny dancer in a tutu and all!

2 other things FYI’s I want to share:

1. You can actually by water bottle ice trays- they look like a shape/size of a roll of coins and when frozen, they pop out and slide into water bottle with ease..This is a new discovery for us and as avid h2o bottle users- for a few $, it was a great investment. Pop a few into bottle and you’re good to go- super easy!! (you just have to remember to fill the ice tray each night!)

2. If using with any sugary or, flavored substance.. one should empty and rinse out bottle once done. Do not let it sit dirty in sink for a day or 2.. I’ve been told it compromises the integrity and taints the inside of the bottle- ever messing up the flavor moving forward. I also heard never to use with alcohol but… Haven't used in that realm- so, i’m sure if flavor won’t dissipate afterwards?

I hope this info can help in your decision… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: Yatoaita Stainless Steel Vacuum Insulated Wide Mouth Water Bottle,Water Bottle with Straw,Insulated Water Bottle with Straw Lid,Wide Mouth Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle (32 oz)

text_fidelity_a: Power Pro Spectra Fiber Braided Fishing Line I LOVE this fishing line. not only is it a good color that blends in well with most fishing environments, but it's crazy strong! I can't always say the same for the rods or reels, but the line rarely ever snaps. I love that it is such a low profile line too. Like the diameter of the line is far thinner than the comparable monofilament version, and MUCH easier to tie than the thick plastic stuff. I find the plastic monofilament stuff is harder to get the knot to hold than the braided lines. Yes it is certainly far more expensive than the monofilament ones, but in my personal opinion, it is worth every penny to pay that little extra and rarely ever have to worry about losing that lunker because your line snapped. I have seen the hooks BEND before this line snaps, which to me is pretty darned impressive.

text_fidelity_a:
Naneu Pro Bravo Medium Military Ops Backpack -Olive Green I did quite a bit of research before purchasing this bag for a 6 week trip through Asia. The first day I really used this bag was during a 12-hour layover in London, where I walked around the city much of the day.

I carried a Canon 40D with two relatively lightweight lenses, spare batteries, filters, and a small notebook. At the end of the day, while waiting at Heathrow for the next flight, I was shocked to notice that the bag was already beginning to fall apart! The outer fabric covering the shoulder straps had already begun to tear. So had the fabric above the zipper on the top pocket. The tear was large enough for someone to stick a hand into the pocket. I inspected the bag closely to see if something had caused these tears, but I concluded that the bag was just a piece of junk. It had begun to unravel itself under the weight of a bag that was not even half-filled!

Not having any emergency repair items on hand, the unraveling continued to get worse over the next day. Finally, I had the bag stitched up in Kerala, India, thinking that would be it. Nope! Bye the next day, the bag had unraveled in other spots as well. I had it stitched up again in Mysore, and then again in Bangalore. Thankfully, these minor fixes cost very little in India. By the time I was almost done with Bangkok, I had bought a small roll of duct tape to keep my items from falling out of the bag. I had also had countless thoughts about the negative review I would write on Amazon when I'd returned home.

I considered writing about the design and functionality of the bag, but there's really no point in doing so.

This bag is a worthless piece of junk. It's amazing that they get away with charging almost $80 for this. Naneu Pro should be ashamed for manufacturing such an inferior product, while marketing itself to be an innovative company that produces high quality goods. I'm truly shocked that Amazon and B&H Photo carry this bag. A $10 bag from the local discount store would have been more durable. What a total ripoff!
text_fidelity_b: Naneu Pro Bravo Medium Military Ops Backpack -Olive Green

text_fidelity_a:
AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking Sometimes where we live, it can get really scary when people drive by quickly and you are trying to go for a walk in the country to just relax. Having this vest handy is really a great item to put on both during the night time or dusk hours, or during hunting season to keep from being shot.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
CLOSURES
This comes with an XL vest that fits around the sides and closes. with strong velcro type closures.

FABRIC
This is a very nice mesh fabric. It allows for airflow and has a slight stretch/give to it so it is comfortable.

SIZING
This fits me and I am between a size 14 and 16 misses. If I were to put this over a winter jacket, I could still close it unless the coat is WAY too puffy.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
POWER BOX
This is ingenious, actually. There is a little packet which recharges. It has a plug on it and also a cord that is USB to recharge it. Once it is charged, then you slip the little box unto a closed pocket which sits under a power button. The box gives a place for the power button to rest on when you press it.

LIGHTS
Once you have it connected, the button is pressed once, and you get the lights on front and back to go on. Once the lights are on, then you can make them flash fast by pressing another time. One more press makes for a slower blink, and a fourth press turns them off.

VEST
The vest itself is brilliant neon yellow. There is plenty of reflective tape all over this vest front and back. There is even a zipper pocket on the front for you to put your phone or other small items in.

BATTERY LIFE?
The battery life of this seems quite good. I have used it a few times and there is still no need for a recharge. I would say you could get a few hours of continuous use at least per charge, maybe more. My outings did not add up to that much yet.

WASHING
I am only going to handwash this without the battery pack and air dry it well before trying to use again. It will dry fast due to the fabric.

HUNTING SEASON
Around my area, fall time into winter can be dangerous. We have had our home shot by hunters by accident, and often there are inexperienced people who try to hunt and they don't pay attention to what is going on, thinking noises are deer. This vest will alert anyone in the early morning or early evening hours that there is a person there.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great vest to have handy. I plan to keep using this especially through hunting season and for late night walks when i hear a car coming.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is an ingenious little invention and I am glad to have it. I am considering purchasing others for the rest of the family.
text_fidelity_b: AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking

text_fidelity_a:
Marcy Folding Standard Weight Bench – Easy Storage MWB-20100, Incline I ordered this weight bench (March MWB-20100 Standard Bench) for my teenager and he loves it. I will first give you his comments and then end the review by giving my own.

A 14-year-old’s honest review:

In high school, I take weight training for PE. I have learned a lot but thought that some equipment at home would really help. So when my mom got this one, I was excited. This weight bench was very easy to put together. And because I couldn’t wait, I put it together myself instead of waiting for my father to get home. All I had to do was match the numbers to the pictures and the only tool I needed was a wrench. It was easy to assemble, only took me about 30 minutes to put together and I’m only 14. Don’t worry my dad did check my work when he got home. You can do a few different things with this bench. You can do the standard lifts or arm/bicep curls. I am 6’2, 159lbs and have really long arms, so it is a little close but is fine for me to use. By close, I am talking about the weight hooks. They are closer than the ones on the equipment I use at school. I also like that you can adjust the seats and back on the bench. This is great for when you work certain areas of the body. The cushions are comfortable and well padded with foam. Beware that this bench does not come with the bar or weights, but I had my mom to go to the local sports store and order some. I got a decent set for under $200. Regardless, I like this bench a lot. It allows me to build a little muscle without having to go to the gym at school. I deducted half a star for the closeness of the hooks.

Now what “mom” likes about this bench:

I liked the fact that he could put this together himself (I’m directionally challenged and his dad wasn’t at home), with very few tools. It occupies some of his time and gives him a productive outlet for teenage frustration and angst (smile). He can close himself in the room, play his music and pump away. And if I am so moved and want a light workout, this set isn’t so overwhelming or complicated that I am too intimidated to use it. BUT THE FEATURE THAT I LOVE AND THE ONE I THINK ALL MOMS WILL LOVE is the fact that by removing one of the pins, you can fold it vertically and it takes up little space. Meaning if you don’t have a basement, and I don’t….and choose to dedicate one room to exercise equipment, you won’t be overwhelmed by the size of it all. I have this bench in my extra bedroom, which is also a computer room. When company comes, or when I want to use the space for something else, I can release, pull up and store it. How fantastic is that?

And finally, as a consumer, this bench appears to be comparably priced with others on the market. When I priced bars and weights, I noticed that the local sports stores were selling the Marcy brand for comparably what Amazon was charging. Marcy is a brand known in the exercise equipment arena. The product appears to be well made and durable. For amateurs and young teens, this would be a decent purchase at under $250. I highly recommend it and give it 4.5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Marcy Folding Standard Weight Bench – Easy Storage MWB-20100, Incline

text_fidelity_a:
Vive Shoulder Pulley - Over Door Rehab Exerciser for Rotator Cuff Recovery I used a version of this device at the physical therapist and this one is a better quality. I tore a muscle in my upper arm (not once but twice!) and both times my shoulder “froze” up from lack of motion while healing.

I found this style to be even more comfortable than what was at therapy, with its nicely padded handles. It looks like (from the seller pictures) they have improved the over-the-door hook, making it easier to reach and hook over the door..

You just need to find a door that allows you to swing your arms in all different directions without running into something.

I prefer sitting on a bar stool or chair but standing also works. I’m standing these days and needed to shorten the cords. I just wrapped them around the soft-padded handles and that worked for me.

I highly recommend this as a good way to keep up with maintaining flexibility. I haven’t been to the physical therapist in a few years, but I still use this device. Not only does it help me stretch and keep more limber, but I notice an improvement in my posture when I use it a few times a week. It also helps tone the areas along my sides and the backs of my upper arms.

Honestly, it only takes me a few minutes to do some basic stretching and see results. If you could find a place to just leave it up all the time, that would make it even more convenient.

I found this to be plenty sturdy and certainly affordable. You might even be able to use your FSA funds to cover the cost.

Certainly easy to pack in a bag when traveling.

It has never damaged my door or frame.

I highly recommend and would purchase again.
text_fidelity_b: Vive Shoulder Pulley - Over Door Rehab Exerciser for Rotator Cuff Recovery

text_fidelity_a:
ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 4-Person Tent, Sage/Rust Having had, and liking, several ALPS Mountaineering products ([[ASIN:B004R7L7YU ALPS OutdoorZ Commander Backpack, 5250 Cubic Inches]] and [[ASIN:B006H1YL1U ALPS Mountaineering Stuff Sack]]), and being in the market for another tent, I chose the 4 Person tent knowing that (1) I'll never really need it to hold four people and (2), I will not be carrying this in my backpack. This tent was specifically bought for car camping.

I like that it has a carry case instead of stuff sack. I'm not quite certain why, but this just seems to make more sense to me. I'm probably less likely to forget the case. I'm also happy with the set up. Instead of sliding poles through a sleeve as several of my other tents do, this is simply a connect the poles, lay them out, put the ends into the stoppers and clip the tent to the poles. It's much easier going up and, if you were in a good location, you really wouldn't need to put in pegs and could freestand.

The one thing about this tent that I didn't like or understand is why they were put a pole under the fly and have you pull the fly up and over the erected tent like that. Honestly, I looked and looked at the instructions and did not see a single thing about that. YouTube came to the rescue in the form of "Mr. Tent".

Since I've not had the opportunity to actually test it out of yet - sure I could put it up in the livingroom and have "Camp InHouse", and I may yet do that, I'm going to leave this review as is and modify it in the future should the need arise. I do not anticipate any problems because I am familiar with the brand, style of tent and my expected usage.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 4-Person Tent, Sage/Rust

text_fidelity_a:
The Flex Belt Abdominal Muscle Toner , Black, 24"-47" Bottom line: If you're looking for a magic solution that will produce firm abs with no effort, keep on looking - this won't do that (nor will anything else!). It is, however, an effective supplement to the usual ab routines. Tha major downside is the price (both initial and on-going).

Full review: Abs are one of the most difficult body parts for me to keep toned since many of the more effective exercises, such as crunches, are difficult for me to do with any degree of intensity due to chronic back problems. This looked like an interesting way to get a low-impact targeting of my abs.

The device is in essence a TENS system. That stands for transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, and is a technique that has been used for years by physical therapists to help alleviate pain. I was first introduced to TENS therapy when I ruptured a disk and needed a few weeks of physical therapy to help with the recovery process. You can do a search on TENS and get all the specific details but in brief it involves placing pads on your body and applying an electrical charge. I know, that sounds rather Frankenstein-ish, but it's safe (if used properly) and not at all unpleasant.

The belt has three pads that it positions on your abs when you put the belt on. You can adjust the pad position based on your waist size. The manual provides clear instructions as to how/where to place the pads. There are also some very nicely done videos on their website to help with setup and usage.

The unit has a control pad that allows you to select the program and vary the intensity. There are 10 different programs that range from 20 to 40 minutes long. There is a wide range of intensity level adjustments (0 to 150) which vary it from "can't feel it at all" to "please stop!!" I was impressed at the number of settings it offers to control the intensity of the stimulation.

I found the controller to be very easy to use, with a clear display that shows the time and intensity level.

The belt is battery powered. You charge it using the supplied AC adapter. Once charged, you do not need to be plugged into the wall outlet to use it - the battery is built into the device. There's an indicator that tells you when the battery power is low and you need to recharge (which takes a few hours). Battery life is good, with each charge lasting for several sessions.

The belt is comfortable to wear and adjusts easily. I was a bit disappointed in the build quality of the belt, however. Given the price I was expecting something that was more robust. It's OK, but it's not something that wow'ed me in terms of construction quality.

There are ongoing costs in using this in that you have to replace the pads at regular intervals (the manufacturer recommends replacement after 30 uses). The replacement pads are pricy ($15), and you'll want to factor that into the total cost of ownership. You can extend the pad life by using electrode gel (such as this: [[ASIN:B0002CA8RQ Spectra 360 Electrode Gel]]. There are many other brands of gel as well). In addition to keeping the pads usable for a longer time, the gel helps increase conductivity (it's also great to use with heart rate monitors).

So, does it work? Yes - I saw an increase in ab definition after using it. However, it comes with a BIG caveat: the belt alone won't give you perfect abs. You still need to watch your diet and do conventional exercises to keep your weight down so that the flab don't hide the abs. The belt will help fine-tune the process by targeting your abs, but the belt alone won't do squat if you're overweight, or expect it to get you into shape you while you sit on the sofa eating chips.

I'll give it 4 stars since it works well and does what it is supposed to do. The manual is clear, and the product is easy to use. The main downside (and the reason for a loss of one star) is that for the price I was expecting more sturdy-feeling components or have it include more accessories, such as the attachments that you can get to target your arms. At the very least it should include a more ample supply of pads (it comes with one set).

Pricy for what you get, but it does what it says it will do.
[the manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: The Flex Belt Abdominal Muscle Toner , Black, 24"-47"

text_fidelity_a:
AXV Vibration Plate Exercise Machine Whole Body Workout Vibrate Fitness Platform Lymphatic Drainage Machine for Weight Loss Shaping Toning Wellness Home Gyms Workout I've wanted one of these vibration platforms for a long time, after reading a book on Whole Body Vibration (WBV) for seniors. That book said not to get an oscillation machine, which this is, because the oscillations can cause injuries that the more expensive machine types don't, but this one is so small I find I'm having no difficulty at all with the oscillations. Put it this way: I could never afford a more expensive machine, and the fact that I was offered this on Vine for review is what made me able to try a WBV platform at all.

This smaller model does not have bluetooth, unlike some of the larger vibration plates offered on AXV's sales page, but that's just fine with me. I wanted something inexpensive and uncomplicated that I can keep by my bed and stand on while watching TV. As my room is arranged, it turns out that my recliner is perfectly positioned to hold onto while I'm standing on the platform for extra stability, and it can sit unobtrusively by the head of my bed so I'm always reminded to use it. I don't even have to stow it away.

The manual that came with this mini vibration plate was plenty detailed in terms of what you can do with this, but it does not have clear explanations of what the different programmed settings do, which I think they should add. Because of my age and the fact that I have osteoporosis, I'm not likely to try the exercises included in the manual except for maybe the biceps curls and calf raises, but these are clearly shown in photographs if you're interested.

When I saw in the answers to customer questions that this machine is manufactured at the same factory as another well-known product, I went to good old YouTube and searched for videos for help. I found "Waver Mini Vibration Platform Orientation" and it looks almost exactly like this product in terms of size and shape. After watching that video, which had a wealth of information about how to use the different programs along with cautionary info for beginners, I'm thinking this machine's programs are set up in a similar way so the advice for the Waver likely applies to this machine as well.

Unlike some of the other WBV machines offered by AXV, this mini has nine programs. I didn't run through all of them, but from trying P0 through P4 and then running a few of the higher programs without standing on the platform, it appears that these programs do coincide with the Waver programs in terms of intensity: first third beginning level, second third intermediate, final third advanced. When a program is running, the selected program number is shown on the left and "14" on the right, which I think means it starts out on a 14 intensity setting out of 99. The P# screen cycles between the program and a from-10-minute countdown number that, when you're in your last minute of WBV, switches to seconds remaining. I found this very helpful.

The only thing I didn't like, and why I knocked off a star, is that the carbiner clips you use to affix the resistance bands kept coming off, probably because they're pretty cheap. I'll probably buy some stainless steel locking ones to be sure the bands don't snap off while I'm using them, because the two times it happened it destabilized my balance and I almost fell. Not a good thing for someone with osteoporosis! Other than that, I think this is a fine value for someone wanting to try a vibration platform, and I think it's just right for seniors. Just make sure you don't weigh over 264 lbs. and, if you do, get a machine rated higher.
text_fidelity_b: AXV Vibration Plate Exercise Machine Whole Body Workout Vibrate Fitness Platform Lymphatic Drainage Machine for Weight Loss Shaping Toning Wellness Home Gyms Workout

Assembly was straightforward and without any issues. In use, it seems well made and sturdy. It's a typical flywheel design with a knob to adjust a resistance onto the wheel itself. The seat is completely adjustable for height and can be position more forward or rearward to further adjust your position relative to the pedals and the handlebars. The seat itself is nicely padded and reasonably comfortable, although I am considering replacing the seat with something wider. It uses a standard bicycle seat, so that should be an easy thing to do.

The pedals are those "steel trap" type with the jagged contacts that require you to wear shoes. I'm okay with that, but theres a nylon strap system that surrounds your toes. My size 12 feet means I'm pedaling on my toes. The pedals, therefore, were the first thing to be replaced. Again, it uses standard picycly parts so replacement was easy.

The control module is a simple battery operated counter. It can track miles, calories or time... or it can be set to cycle through the various measurements as you go. Theres no connection to the adjustable wheel resistance, so things like calorie burn are obviously just an approximation, at best. But that's pretty typical, I'm sure.

Overall, I recommend this bike. It seems well made and it gets the job done.

Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Exercise Bike Ordered this from Amazon December 20, 2015 and it was delivered the following Sunday. I assembled the bike a few hours after it arrived without troubles.

For some reason there is a full page parts diagram of the entire bike that is shown prior to the assembly instructions. The diagram made things look way more complicated than they turned out to be. Turns out (most) of the hardware is already in place and just needs to be aligned and tightened (with the included tools).

I assembled this on my own and most people should be able to do just like I did. One note on assembly though: the main part of this is the bulk of the total weight of the entire bike. It's a bit on the heavy side so if lifting heavy objects is hard or risky for you you should seek out some help.

The pedals went on super quick and easy. They were clearly marked 'L' and 'R' and the instructions made sure there were clear on which way the bolts should be threaded.

I've since put 320 miles on the odometer on this, so, about 14.5 miles a day. I haven't noticed any mechanical problems or glaring defects. I enjoy the fact the the seat is adjustable to some degree and the adjustable tension works surprisingly well.

My reason for giving only four stars is because of the seat. It is very hard and after a while it causes pain. I'm going to get a nice cover for it and hopefully that will help some with that.

Other than that, this is a great bike for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Exercise Bike

text_fidelity_a:
YADEA Electric Scooter Adults, Foldable Commuting Electric Scooters KS5, 3 Adjustable Speeds Max 18.6 MPH, 25 Miles Long Range, Dual Shock Absorption, Front Suspension, Triple Brake, Cruise Control I just purchased the KS5 Pro. Here are my comparisons with the KS5.

Larger deck. Both feet fit more comfortably. Heavier. Harder to move around but feels sturdier when riding. Problems with rear fender appear to be solved (see old review). Extra bracing metal stops fender from flopping around like on my KS5. Handlebars are 2-3” higher than the KS5. This is a scooter that should be able to handle 6’6” riders easy…

Max speed drops approx 20% when at two bars and 30% when at one bar. Ex: my max speed when riding in sport mode at one bar is 13-15mph on flats. Max downhill speed is 22mph

My KS5 delivers almost full speed up until one flashing bar...

Max range is about 19 miles.

I weigh 220lbs.

Overall this is a great and sturdy scooter that reduces range anxiety and should be able to get you anywhere within a city.

Note: initially my regen brakes would cut on fully (and seemingly randomly) when I put very light pressure on the brakes. This would happen once for every ~50 times I hit the brakes. This lead to unexpected moments where I would almost get thrown off the scooter. Completely unexpected and super dangerous. I'm very experienced at scootering, skateboarding, biking, and this almost wiped me out each time. This happened for the first week, then suddenly stopped. I had just set the scooter up for return shipping and my last ride (to be completely sure) did not have the problem.

——————-old KS5 review—————-
Update: I’m on my fourth rear fender. They break under normal road vibration. Fracture, crack, break at the base where the fender rises from the deck of the scooter. Four different fenders. No collisions or crashes. This one part needs a redesign.

———————

When the scooter first arrived I was VERY impressed by the build and weight. This thing is a beauty. Ship packaging was adequate with lots of cardboard keeping everything separate and stationary.

Assembly was very simple. Just a few screws to attach and an app to download from the IOS appstore.

Second impression was pretty poor however. Could not get the handlebar post straight - even with max strength. And could not get the headlights to turn on without first using the phone app.

Turns out both were my mistake (and somewhat the fault of the mediocre documentation/startup docs).

You can't access any scooter functions while its charging. So when you first open the box and logically go to charge it, double-tapping to turn on the headlights won't work. You may also need to adjust the screw at the base of the handlebar post. It used a different Allan key size than the included key, but tightening it up a bit will make it easier to open/close.

The app is sufficient. It definitely could use some user interface redesign - its lost opportunity to turn this into an exceptional product - but it suffices for what it is. I set the unit to hi regen on braking and "baby mode" for my first test runs.

Tires are hard. There is some give - but these feel pretty much like solid tires to me. If there is a honeycomb design inside, it will likely show itself on the most heinous road bumps and not by simply pushing a finger or pen into the tire material.

Shocks were pretty sticky when I tested them in my house. Not smooth at all. They loosened up considerably after a 5K test run. And about that test run...

I rode to a smooth track near my house and did about 10 laps. On the perfect surface I was able to focus on the acceleration and handling of the scooter. Very, very good. In S mode has a great pickup, and I achieved MAX speed in a few seconds. Braking was very good. I immediately came to a stop with double as well as single brakes. Regen seemed to bring me to a stop - but was not very aggressive feeling - even on max. That might be due to my weight.

I am a fit 215lbs and am 6' tall. Size 11 feet. The scooter feels like it was built for me. Deck is plenty spacious and handlebar grips are at the perfect height for me. I've been on scooters that felt fragile - this is NOT one of them. I pulled on the bars as I cornered and pushed on them as I braked. No wiggle. No squeek.

After the smooth track, I went to a nearby jacked-up parking lot, filled with cracks, weeds and bumps. The scooter handled 1" lips and 2-3" gaps in pavement well. The shocks did their jobs, but the wheels gave me little joy. I felt significant road vibration. Maybe the wheels need a break in period as well...

As for the weight and storage ... I commute using a folding bike (Dahon Vigor D9) and this scooter weighs significantly more (50%) and is much harder to handle when walking it or when folded. I've gotten into a habit of taking my Dahon with me everywhere possible and I fold it down quickly and roll it around or pick it up when I need to.

This is a bulky scooter and you won't want to pick it up and carry it often. I was able to use it as an unpowered kick scooter pretty easily. So running out of power when on the road should not be a problem. But multimodal commuting might be annoying if you have a lot of stairs to climb or will be on a tight train.

The charge outlet is well-protected with a spring loaded cap. There is also some rubber backing in the cap to help create a better water seal. Should be good for splashes. But I'd stay away from a puddle deep enough to immerse the bottom of the board.

The front and rear lights are very bright. No additional lights are needed.

Changes?

Improve the quality of the app. Make it so good/informative that people will want it open on the handlebar of the scooter while they're riding. Do more quality control of the text as well.

Maybe provide wheels with a tiny bit more cushion. Wheel tech is steadily improving and a softer core wheel (keep it solid) will definitely make folks happier. I can't imagine anyone wanting harder wheels.

Improve your documentation and startup tips card. Larger font. Clearer layout. Put things in order of importance for the best startup experience. A large, colorful startup tips card that says things like (lights won't turn on when charging, adjust handlebar base, etc). And change the screw on the handlebar base to the same size Allan key as the rest of the screws on the scooter. I have tools, some may not.

Excellent scooter and highly recommended!

----------------

Update:

Today I went for a 10 mile ride. I used ECO for 75% and SPORT mode for 25%. MAX speed almost all the way. There were three significant uphills (1/4 mile each) and several large downhills. I used regenerative braking as much as possible. When I got home I had 1 bar left, flashing.

I weight 215 lbs, which is approaching the upper limit of the scooter's spec. So on a full charge I can reliably get about 10 miles out of the scooter judiciously using SPORT mode. For me, this scooter is good since my office is 3 miles away from my house. I can just blast on SPORT both ways.

Since I've owned the scooter the APP has gone through an update adding a few new features. Its still pretty poor quality and does not seem to save my changes to settings like regenerative braking, etc.

------UPDATE-------

I've lowered the star rating by one due to the following issues.

1. Noise. The rear fender makes a LOT of noise when riding. Constant clunking sounds as it flops around. Its very irritating. They also break under the vibration load. I’M ON MY FOURTH REAR FENDER UNDER WARRANTY!!! AND IT JUST BROKE AS WELL. THEY ALL CRACK AND THEN BREAK AT THE SAME SPOT!!!

2. Range anxiety. From a full charge, the scooter drops down to one flashing bar at 8.5 miles on me, regularly. Far short of 25 miles and I'm wistful... It would make sense that the flashing bar is really 25% power remaining instead of 10% or less - but I don't want to test it. I usually need 10 miles of range when I ride the scooter (its a round trip) and I can just eek it out if I only use sport mode for the first 10-20% of my ride (when I need more speed to better negotiate car traffic). By the time I'm heading home using standard mode exclusively I'm stressing range. So I guess I can lose 15 lbs to get better range... Carrying the charger and recharging on the road is not an option in this use case.

3. Accelerator glitches. The scooter has gunned uncontrollably on two occasions. Both times I was sitting at a light, then I pressed the accelerator and the scooter took off at max speed and would not stop, even when I hit the brakes! I had to turn off the power... The first time I thought it was something I did. Second time I realized it was the scooter. VERY dangerous situations for me both times. I can only guess that it may have something to do with cruise control as it did not happen before I turned that on (may be coincidental). I'll turn off cruise control for the time being when riding in traffic/pedestrian settings and will try to replicate the issue in a parking lot and see if its some type of user error...

4. Aftermarket service has been excellent thus far. Yadea have sent me replacement parts for the rear fender. As well as PDF and video instructions on maintenance. Very responsive to requests. Scooter front shocks are still quite sticky. Can’t seem to lube or adjust them to be smoother. Side reflectors are a pain to get off in order to service rear wheel or replace rear fender. However, once you have performed maintenance on the scooter, repeat sessions are easy.
text_fidelity_b: YADEA Electric Scooter Adults, Foldable Commuting Electric Scooters KS5, 3 Adjustable Speeds Max 18.6 MPH, 25 Miles Long Range, Dual Shock Absorption, Front Suspension, Triple Brake, Cruise Control

SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag Waterproof Accessory for Paddle Boarding If the devil is in the details this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag is made with a range of details that make it an outstanding, well thought out bag, and should be perfect for our Kayaking and SUPing trips. We haven’t been out on the water yet this year, but cannot wait to get back out and without doubt, this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag will be going along for the ride! When I had the chance to grab this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag I decided to so we had a nice bag to carry those things we might need on the water and have a place to keep our phone, wallets, and keys safe. I am so glad I did - and my wife is thrilled. This bag was designed by someone who has time on the water and it shows.

The materials are top notch and the construction equally great. You can tell by looking at the bag the materials are good. But get your hands on it and you feel it. The thickness, the strength, the stitching - it all comes together and promises longevity. We always pay attention to zippers and in this case, not only is the handle-zipper strong and secure, but it settles in perfectly so as to keep water out. There are the details here - straps on the back top at each side so you can grab and hold on as you “try” to open and close the zipper. It literally warns you it is a hard pull and it is! That simply means water is going to be working hard to get in there. And the straps do help pull it across - though you’re still going to be grabbing the bag at some point to help. It is that tight! No problem if it means protecting your gear. They even included zipper lube so you can keep those zippers in top condition - something to keep in mind when you’re on fresh or salt water! Really impressive they thought of these things!

The strap for carrying it is also well done, with good materials, good stitching, and a comfortable padding on the shoulder. The straps for attaching to the SUP or Kayak are strong and well secured - they should last a good long time. Additionally, the rope on the top front allows you to secure things like towels, tighten it down, and keep them secure. An included wet bag for your phone gives added protection for that special need-to-have equipment.

Overall, this is a great, well designed bag that I think anyone who spends time on the water will appreciate. Well thought out, well constructed, and well executed, you are going to find any number of reasons to have it with - on the SUP or kayak, at the pool, beach, or wherever you spend time. We have not tested the waterproof aspect - again, haven’t been to the water yet, but while we appreciate the promise, we always still try to keep things dry. We would likely use other smaller dry bags inside - just to be safe - but appreciate the effort here. In the end, we are thrilled to have this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag.
text_fidelity_b: SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag Waterproof Accessory for Paddle Boarding

text_fidelity_a:
TFO Air Camping Sleeping Pad 1lb Ultralight, Upgraded 40D Tear-Resistant Nylon, Textured Inflatable Camping Mat with Compact Carrying Bag for Backpacking/Hiking The Earth is the world's largest heat sink & everyone who has slept on the ground knows that the earth will suck all the heat from your body as you try to sleep. This mat rolls up very compact, fills quickly & breaks down quickly. It is superior in every way to the pool float a lot of people (myself included) use.

This mat uses dozens of little chambers instead one big one which makes it fill faster & breaks down easier. The fill valve does not have a protrusion like a straw or a nipple, rather I kind of had to "kiss" it to blow it up. I was able to blow it up in about 65 seconds (I timed it). The port has a check valve that works very well so the air stays inside the mattress. The valve flaps around a bit & makes a squeaking sound that my wife compared to a Wookie.

To deflate, the valve opens to a 1" diameter hole. Because of the multiple air chambers, air does not get trapped in the rolled end when rolling it up. This makes a huge difference because it can be folded before all of the air is out. It took me 2 minutes to deflate, roll & bag the mat. Of course this is in my living room & not in 2-person tent.

I confess that I haven't slept on this mat yet but I did lay & roll around on it. It is just as noisy as my Thermarest mat and feels about the same thickness. It's not uncomfortable but also not particularly supple. It is on par for this type of low-profile, inflatable mat.

I usually tent-camp off my motorcycle where weight isn't so important but space is. This mat is way more compact than any of my other mats. If I was tent camping from the car I would probably stick with my self-inflating mat but this will definitely go on my next motorcycle trip. It is very light, probably light enough for hiking or biking but I can't speak to that.
text_fidelity_b: TFO Air Camping Sleeping Pad 1lb Ultralight, Upgraded 40D Tear-Resistant Nylon, Textured Inflatable Camping Mat with Compact Carrying Bag for Backpacking/Hiking

The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
825 cubic inches
16 1/2” x 10” x 5”
6” mesh pockets – smaller pockets
Covers about 4 ¾” of bottles
Straps 2 ¼” wide
This pack has 3 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a middle sized zippered compartment. In the front is a small zippered pocket.
Pros:
- Small zippered pocket inside the main compartment. This is where the pack is stored when folded.
- Very easy to adjust shoulder straps
- Reinforced mesh straps feel soft and pliable
- Pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying pack
Cons:
- Thinner material than a standard backpack.
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.

I ordered one of these for myself in a different color.
text_fidelity_b: Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L

text_fidelity_a: Kalili 9 inch Lengthen Aluminum Alloy Y shaped Tent Stakes Tent Pegs for Camping Hiking 10 Pcs These 9-inch stakes are a welcome upgrade from the ubiquitous 7-inch versions, and offered at a reasonable price (at least when I bought them). These longer stakes work well in soft to moderately firm soil, but you still have to take care not to pound them too hard into rocks or solid tree roots or they'll bend. I like to use them with smaller tents on the windward side of the tent, to give a little better holding power than the shorter stakes offer, and on the sheltered side of larger tents, where you don't need such a strong hold (with longer stakes on the windward side). The supplied cord loops are a nice touch, making it easy to see and pull your stakes when it's time to go. Many suppliers don't include those cord loops, but I think it's a good investment to add them if they aren't included, so you're less likely to lose the stakes (because you can see the bright loops, and they make a good handle for pulling the stakes from the ground).

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos The Sabre Red Runner Pepper Gel personal alarm is a product you don’t want to review after having to use it.  But looking it over thoroughly I find it to be very well thought out.  It’s about the size of a tube of mascara yet weighs less.  Hardly noticeable when strapped to my arm.  The comfortable adjustable strap and uncomplicated trigger safety – just slide the red trigger over about half an inch then push to spray – make it appear to be simple to use, even in a frightened state.  But what I like best is the alarm that comes with it.  It has a very sturdy clip that can be successfully attached to a flimsy T-shirt or a fairly thick coat.  There is a green light that has three options: On, Slow flash, and Fast flash.  The light is also used to test the battery.  Holding the light button down for 3 seconds and seeing if the light quickly flashes green or red indicates battery strength.  The four LR44 batteries (included) can be replaced.  I think the alarm alone would deter most criminals.  To say it’s loud is an understatement.  The brochure states to avoid prolonged exposure as it could cause permanent hearing loss.  I’d recommend trying this away from children and pets.  It is painfully loud!  I hope I never need it but I’m glad I have it.
